name: Mark Miller
current_role: President and Chief Operating Officer, Constellation Software (CSI); director, CSI board; executive chairman of Volaris Group
profile: Canadian software executive who co-founded transit-software firm Trapeze Group in 1988; it became Constellation Software's first acquisition in 1995. He built Volaris Group, a CSI operating group that has bought 200+ vertical-market software companies, and now serves as CSI President/COO and board member. Owns ~1% of CSI plus Topicus and Lumine shares.
interesting_fact: Trapeze, the transit-planning software company he co-founded, was the very first company Constellation Software ever acquired (1995); its name came from the tagline 'Transit Planning Made Easy'.
deep_cut_fact: Studied math and statistics at McMaster; spent summers coding on mainframes at the Canada Centre for Inland Waters (Great Lakes water research). He and co-founder Ian Keaveny taught themselves C from the Kernighan & Ritchie book to build Trapeze; first sale was in St. John's, Newfoundland, where he coded on site.
notes: Input SEC insider data (UHS CEO / Premier director) belongs to a different person (Marc D. Miller of Universal Health Services) - ignore. CSI management page lists Miller as President and COO; corporate email info@csisoftware.com is generic.

name: Lee Sang-hoon
current_role: Founder, Chairman, CEO and Chief Research Officer, ABL Bio (Kosdaq-listed, South Korea)
profile: Korean scientist-entrepreneur who founded bispecific-antibody developer ABL Bio in February 2016 and listed it on Kosdaq in 2018. A November 2025 tech-transfer deal with Eli Lilly worth up to $2.6B for its Grabody-B blood-brain-barrier platform sent shares soaring and made him a billionaire. He continues to lead R&D for oncology and neurodegeneration programs.
interesting_fact: ABL Bio was born after Hanwha Chemical decided to shut down the biotech division Lee headed; he spun out with colleagues and built ABL Bio, later landing a $2.6B Eli Lilly deal for its brain-shuttle antibody technology.
deep_cut_fact: Before biotech he trained as a teacher: his B.S. from Seoul National University is in Biology Education. He then earned a PhD at Ohio State, did postdocs at Harvard Medical School and Stanford, worked at Chiron, AstraZeneca, Genentech and Exelixis, and co-founded PharmAbcine before ABL Bio.
notes: Country in input is United States, but he is Korean and based in Seoul (ABL Bio HQ, Seongnam). Speaks at BIO International; member of Council of Korean Americans.

name: Michael Kors
current_role: Honorary Chairman and Chief Creative Officer, Michael Kors (brand of Capri Holdings)
profile: New York-born fashion designer who launched his womenswear line in 1981 at Bergdorf Goodman and built it into a global accessible-luxury brand; the company IPO'd in 2011 and became Capri Holdings (also owner of Jimmy Choo). He was creative director of Celine (1997-2004) and a Project Runway judge, and still leads design for his namesake brand.
interesting_fact: He co-founded Watch Hunger Stop with the UN World Food Programme in 2013, funding school meals worldwide; he is also a longtime board member of NYC meals charity God's Love We Deliver.
deep_cut_fact: After dropping out of FIT after nine months, his first job was at Lothar's, a boutique on West 57th Street, where he went from salesman to designer and window dresser; Bergdorf Goodman's Dawn Mello spotted him while he was merchandising the windows, leading to his 1981 Bergdorf debut.
notes: Fashion figure rather than energy/tech; best route is Capri Holdings press office. Instagram @michaelkors is the brand account, not personal.

name: Chen Haibin
current_role: Chairman and controlling shareholder, Dian Diagnostics Group (迪安诊断, SZSE: 300244), Hangzhou
profile: Hangzhou entrepreneur (b. 1969, CEIBS EMBA) who started a diagnostics business in 1996 and founded Dian in 2001; it listed on Shenzhen's ChiNext in 2011 and grew into one of China's largest independent clinical laboratory networks, combining lab services with IVD product distribution. Chairman since 2019 (previously also GM); remains the controlling shareholder as of 2026.
interesting_fact: He attended Jack Ma's Hupan University (湖畔大学) entrepreneur program; Dian, which marks its 30th anniversary in 2026, frames its expansion around a 'bamboo forest' (竹林) strategy of interconnected businesses.
deep_cut_fact: Per his own shareholder letter, the business began in 1996 in a bare ~30 m2 office in Hangzhou; less than two years in, a national clean-up of the PCR testing market forced a pivot to independent medical laboratories - the 'products + services' model Dian is built on.
notes: Former Zhejiang CPPCC member; chairs the Zhejiang Health Industry Federation. IR/board secretary (Tao Jun) is the realistic route; Chinese-language outreach advised.

name: Zhuang Chenchao
current_role: Founder of Banma Capital (斑马投资) and founder of data-driven convenience-store chain Bianlifeng (便利蜂), Beijing
profile: Shanghai-born (1976) Peking University electronics graduate who co-founded travel search site Qunar in 2005 and served as its CEO until it merged with Ctrip in 2015. He left in January 2016 to start investment firm Banma (Zebra) Capital and, later that year, Bianlifeng, an algorithm-run convenience-store chain. Also an early investor in Rong360 and Meilishuo.
interesting_fact: Bianlifeng was built around his 'mathematical thinking': store ordering, pricing and staffing are largely decided by algorithms rather than store managers.
deep_cut_fact: While still a PKU student he built a search engine, Souke (搜索客), in November 1997; in 1999 he co-founded sports site Sharkwhy (鲨威) as CTO with Fritz Demopoulos, then worked as a systems architect at the World Bank in Washington before reuniting with Demopoulos to found Qunar.
notes: Input 'Banma' refers to his Banma (Zebra) investment vehicle, not Alibaba's Banma auto-OS JV. Keeps a low public profile; no published personal or office contact found. Search rate limits cut research short; current Bianlifeng role not re-verified for 2026.

name: Shan Weijun
current_role: Chairman and CEO, Auntea Jenny (沪上阿姨, HKEX: 2589), Shanghai
profile: Co-founder, with his wife Zhou Rongrong, of Auntea Jenny, one of China's largest fresh-fruit tea chains with well over 6,000 mostly franchised stores. The couple left jobs at a foreign-invested company in Shandong in 2011 to start a business in Shanghai; the brand listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange main board on 8 May 2025.
interesting_fact: Auntea Jenny became the sixth mainland Chinese tea-drink company to list publicly when it debuted in Hong Kong in May 2025; it has since added a coffee sub-brand (沪咖) and a sub-10-yuan brand, Cha Pubu (茶瀑布), for lower-tier cities.
deep_cut_fact: The first Auntea Jenny store opened on 18 July 2013 at Shanghai's People's Square, originally selling Shanghai-style freshly boiled five-grain teas; its breakout hit was a purple 'blood glutinous rice' (血糯米) milk tea that pushed the store past RMB 400,000 in monthly sales.
notes: Fortune shared with wife Zhou Rongrong. No published IR/press email found; company secretaries per HKEX filings are Wang Juan and Yu Anne. Chinese-language outreach advised.

name: Zhen Lixin
current_role: Founder, Chairman and General Manager, INTSIG Information (合合信息, STAR Market: 688615), Shanghai
profile: Pattern-recognition PhD (Chinese Academy of Sciences Institute of Automation, 2000) from Jingzhou, Hubei, who spent nearly a decade at Motorola's China research institute before founding INTSIG in 2006. INTSIG makes CamScanner (扫描全能王), CamCard (名片全能王) and Qixinbao, plus OCR/AI document-processing tech for enterprises; it listed on Shanghai's STAR Market in September 2024.
interesting_fact: CamScanner had more than 1.1 billion registered users worldwide by end-2023, making INTSIG one of China's few consumer apps with a large global user base.
deep_cut_fact: At Motorola China Research Institute he specialised in OCR, business-card and handwriting recognition for touchscreen phones - tech used in Motorola's landmark 'Ming' (明) smartphone series. Six of INTSIG's seven core founding members were his former Motorola research colleagues.
notes: Technical founder, gave interviews to ifanr/TechCrunch Shanghai in early CamCard days. marketing@intsig.com is the company's generic published contact (not specifically press).

name: Constantine Logothetis
current_role: Non-executive board member, Libra Group; Chairman, Alithea Capital; Concordia Leadership Council member
profile: Greek-British shipping heir who joined the family's London firm Lomar Shipping in 2000 and co-founded diversified conglomerate Libra Group with brother George in 2003 as founding Executive Vice Chairman. He led Libra's diversification from shipping into hotels, real estate and renewable energy, stepped back from the executive role in 2017, and now chairs Alithea Capital.
interesting_fact: Libra Group, which he co-founded, operates in ~60 countries across aerospace, renewable energy, maritime, hospitality and real estate; in early 2026 he relocated to the UAE to support the group's push into the Middle East.
deep_cut_fact: He was at the forefront of turning a shipping family business into a multi-sector group, personally driving Libra's moves into renewable energy and hospitality; in Feb 2026 he hosted a Concordia dinner in Abu Dhabi for the nonpartisan forum Libra founded-sponsors.
notes: Relevant to energy angle (Libra's renewable/aerospace interests). Libra's public pages say he resides in London, though a Feb 2026 release says he recently relocated to the UAE. Fortune shared with brother George Logothetis (Libra Executive Chairman / board vice-chair). office@libra.com is Libra Group's generic published address.

name: Lyu Jiangming
current_role: Actual controller (controlling shareholder), Top Choice Medical (通策医疗, SSE: 600763); stepped down as chairman and director in April 2024
profile: Hangzhou entrepreneur (b. 1965) who made his first fortune in property development, then in 2006 bought Hangzhou Stomatology Hospital and took it public via a reverse merger, creating Top Choice Medical. He built it into China's leading private dental-hospital group, chairing it for 18 years before handing the chair to Wang Yi in 2024; he remains its controlling shareholder.
interesting_fact: Top Choice became so profitable that investors nicknamed it 'Ya Mao' (牙茅, the 'Moutai of teeth'); its market value once topped RMB 130 billion.
deep_cut_fact: His jump from real estate to healthcare began in 2006 when he paid about RMB 100 million for Hangzhou Stomatology Hospital and listed it via shell company ST Zhongyan; from 2006 to 2022 revenue grew from RMB 23 million to RMB 2.7 billion.
notes: Input name 'Lyu Jiangming' = 吕建明 (Lü Jianming). Has faced CSRC Zhejiang regulatory warnings (2022, 2024) over related-party funds - avoid in outreach. IR email is board secretary Zhang Hua's, per 2025 annual report (published Apr 2026).

name: Cheong Chiu Ying
current_role: Chairman of the Board, L.K. Technology Holdings (力勁科技, HKEX: 0558), Hong Kong
profile: Chairs L.K. Technology, the Hong Kong-listed maker of die-casting machines, injection-moulding machines and CNC machining centres founded in 1979 by Liu Siong Song (劉相尚). name: Hou Bo-ming
current_role: Chairman, Tainan Spinning Co. (台南紡織, TWSE: 1440) and head of the Tainan Spinning group, Taiwan
profile: Taiwanese industrialist (b. 1955), grandson of Tainan Spinning co-founder Hou Yu-li of the 'Tainan Gang' business clan. He joined Tainan Spinning in 1989, rose through finance to president in 2001 and became chairman in 2016. Under him the textile group has pivoted toward property - the T.S. Mall in Tainan - and a technology park on a former fibre-plant site.
interesting_fact: He is converting Tainan Spinning's shuttered Rende chemical-fibre plant into a roughly 46-jia (~45 ha) Tainan Spinning Science Park, pitched at 5G and tech tenants.
deep_cut_fact: A tourism graduate of Chinese Culture University, he began his career in 1984 at food giant Uni-President (統一企業) before joining Tainan Spinning in 1989 as an assistant manager in the audit team; as president from 2001 he restructured the product mix and returned the company to profit.
notes: Taiwan-based (input says China). Company website did not respond; IR contact should be available via Taiwan MOPS filings. Vice-chairman Hou Bo-yu (侯博裕) is a relative - do not contact via family.

name: Weston Nichols
current_role: Founder and Managing Partner, Lynx1 Capital Management (Puerto Rico-based biotech fund); independent director, Crinetics Pharmaceuticals
profile: Biotech hedge-fund manager (age 41 per 2026 proxy) who founded Lynx1 Capital in 2020 after analyst stints at Perceptive Advisors and Balyasny. Through Lynx1 Master Fund he holds 10%+ stakes in Cullinan Therapeutics, Korro Bio and TScan Therapeutics, and has sat on Crinetics' board since 2018.
interesting_fact: He joined the Crinetics board in 2018 while still an analyst at Perceptive Advisors; the company has since become a commercial-stage endocrinology drugmaker.
deep_cut_fact: A scientist before an investor: he holds a B.S. in biological engineering from Cornell and a Ph.D. in biology from Caltech, and broke into finance in 2014 as a biotech equity research associate at SunTrust Robinson Humphrey.
notes: Net worth figure derives from fund-held stakes (he disclaims beneficial ownership beyond his pecuniary interest), so personal wealth is likely overstated. Lynx1 is based in Dorado, Puerto Rico per SEC Form 4s; no website or published contact found. Low public profile.
